chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he said:
Regarding the man who yawns and stretches during the prayer, he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is from Satan, and he has no control over it.'

key_terms.وَلَا يَمْلِكُهُ: and he has no control over it

ai.seo_question: Why is yawning during prayer considered from Satan?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, the Imam identifies yawning during prayer as a manifestation of Satan's influence, noting its involuntary nature which renders it a sign of spiritual distraction rather than intentional disrespect. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on maintaining khushu' (humility and focus) by actively countering these physical manifestations of heedlessness. It serves as a practical guideline for worshippers to recognize and mitigate the subtle disruptions that can diminish the quality of their connection with the Divine.
